items.text: Under the MIOSHA General Duty Clause, when no specific standard covers a hazard, what must every employer provide?

A. A workplace free from recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious harm — MCL 408.1011 requires every employer to furnish a workplace free from recognized hazards likely to cause death or serious physical harm; it applies when no specific standard covers the hazard.
What does MIOSHA Construction Part 1 require every construction employer to develop and maintain with employees?

C. An accident prevention program — R 408.40114 (Construction Part 1, General Rules) requires every construction employer to develop, maintain, and coordinate an accident prevention program with employees.
A guardrail system is being built at a floor opening. What top rail height and strength are required?

B. 42 inches plus or minus 3 inches, withstanding 200 pounds — Part 45 (adopting 29 CFR 1926.502) sets the top rail at 42 inches plus or minus 3 inches above the walking surface, able to withstand 200 lb of outward or downward force.
What is the maximum free fall distance allowed for a personal fall arrest system?
D. 6 feet — Part 45 (adopting 1926.502) limits PFAS free fall to 6 feet and requires the system to prevent contact with a lower level.
What is the minimum rated strength of a personal fall arrest anchorage point per attached worker?
C. 5,000 pounds — Part 45 (adopting 1926.502(d)) requires anchorages rated at 5,000 lb per attached worker.
On a steep-slope residential roof, conventional fall protection is infeasible at one specific location. What is the compliant fallback?

A. A written site-specific fall protection plan — Part 45 requires conventional systems at 6 feet on steep-slope residential roofs; where infeasible at a specific location, a written site-specific fall protection plan is the fallback.
A worker needs more reach from a portable extension ladder. Which practice violates MIOSHA Part 11?
B. Standing on the top 3 feet of the ladder — R 408.41124 prohibits standing on the top 3 feet of a portable ladder; the other choices are all required or permitted practices.
How much clearance must a portable ladder maintain from power transmission or distribution lines?
D. 20 feet — R 408.41124 requires 20 feet minimum clearance for portable ladders near power lines — a different number from the 10-foot equipment clearance, a classic swap trap.
A crane is working near an overhead power line energized at 45 kilovolts. What minimum clearance applies to the equipment?
A. 10 feet — Equipment must keep 10 feet of clearance from lines up to 50 kV (add 4 inches per 10 kV above 50 kV); the 20-foot figure applies to portable ladders, not equipment.
What rung spacing does MIOSHA require on a ladder?
B. Uniform, 10 to 14 inches apart — R 408.41113 requires uniform rung spacing of 10 to 14 inches.
At what elevation break between working levels must a ladder or other means of access be provided?
C. 19 inches or more — R 408.41113 requires a ladder or other access at any elevation break of 19 inches or more.
A scaffold must be designed to support how much weight?
A. Four times the maximum intended load — Part 12 requires scaffolds to be designed to support 4 times the maximum intended load.
A laborer climbs the cross-braces to reach a scaffold platform. Which statement is correct?
C. Prohibited - safe access such as a ladder, stair, or ramp is required — R 408.41211 requires safe access (ladder, stair, or ramp) and prohibits climbing cross-braces.
What fall protection is required on a two-point adjustable suspension scaffold?
D. Both a personal fall arrest system and a guardrail — R 408.41213 requires both PFAS and a guardrail on single-point and two-point adjustable suspension scaffolds.
A trench is only 4 feet deep, but examination indicates hazardous earth movement may be expected. Is protection required?
B. Yes - protection is still required when hazardous earth movement may be expected — R 408.40941 requires protection under 5 feet when examination indicates hazardous earth movement may be expected.
After a heavy rainstorm overnight, what must happen before crews re-enter an open trench?
C. A competent person must re-inspect the excavation — R 408.40932(4) requires the competent person to re-inspect after every rainstorm or other hazard-producing occurrence.
An excavation cuts through previously disturbed soil. What is the highest soil classification it can receive?
C. Type B — Previously disturbed soil can never be Type A; Type B expressly includes previously disturbed soils (0.5 to 1.5 tsf).
What is the maximum allowable slope for a trench in Type A soil?
D. Three-quarters horizontal to one vertical, 53 degrees — Type A soil (most stable, 1.5 tsf or more) may be sloped at 3/4H:1V, which is 53 degrees; 45 degrees is Type B and 34 degrees is Type C.
During utility locating, the ground is marked with yellow paint. What is buried there?
A. Gas, oil, or steam lines — MISS DIG marking colors: yellow is gas/oil, red electric, blue water, orange telecom, green sewer (PA 174 of 2013 system).
A generator powers 120-volt extension cords on site. Instead of GFCI protection, what alternative does MIOSHA Part 17 allow?

B. An assured equipment grounding conductor program with scheduled testing — R 408.41722 requires GFCI protection OR an Assured Equipment Grounding Conductor Program (AEGCP) with scheduled testing and documentation for 120-volt, 15- and 20-ampere non-permanent receptacles.
What does MIOSHA Part 1 require for first aid on a construction worksite?

C. A person with a valid first aid training certificate present at the worksite — R 408.40132 requires a person holding a valid first aid training certificate (Red Cross or equivalent) to be present at the worksite to render first aid.
What is the permissible exposure limit for respirable crystalline silica?
B. 50 micrograms per cubic meter, 8-hour average — The silica PEL is 50 micrograms per cubic meter (8-hr TWA); 25 is the action level, a listed trap value (fed 1926.1153, adopted).
A subcontractor brings an epoxy product on site. Who must have the safety data sheet accessible?

D. The site must have an SDS readily accessible during the shift for every hazardous chemical present, regardless of who brought it — Under hazard communication (Right to Know), an SDS must be on site and readily accessible during the shift for every hazardous chemical present, regardless of who brought it.
A MIOSHA inspector arrives and the employer refuses entry. What must MIOSHA do to proceed?
A. Obtain a warrant — MCL 408.1029 - if entry is denied, MIOSHA must obtain a warrant; the employer may demand one.
How much advance notice does an employer normally receive before a MIOSHA inspection?

B. None - advance notice is generally prohibited, and unauthorized advance notice is itself an offense — MCL 408.1029 - no advance notice in the ordinary case; giving unauthorized advance notice is itself an offense under the Act.
What is the maximum civil penalty for a willful or repeat MIOSHA violation, and the willful minimum?
C. $70,000 maximum, $5,000 willful minimum — MCL 408.1035 sets willful/repeat penalties at up to $70,000 per violation with a $5,000 willful minimum; federal inflation-adjusted amounts do not apply.
A willful MIOSHA violation causes an employee's death. What is the first-offense criminal exposure?
D. Felony - up to 1 year and a $10,000 fine — MCL 408.1035 makes a willful violation causing death a felony: up to 1 year and/or $10,000 (second offense up to 3 years and/or $20,000).
When must the MIOSHA 300A annual summary be posted, and through what date?
A. Not later than February 1, kept up through April 30 — R 408.22132 requires the 300A annual summary to be posted not later than February 1 and kept up through April 30.
A builder had 8 employees all of last year. A worker suffers an amputation. Which statement is correct?

B. Exempt from routine recordkeeping logs, but must still report the amputation within 24 hours — R 408.22103(1)(a) exempts employers with 10 or fewer employees from routine recordkeeping, but never from the 8-hour fatality and 24-hour hospitalization/amputation/eye-loss reports (R 408.22139).
Before workers enter a confined space such as a deep utility vault, what must occur first?
D. Atmospheric testing before entry — Confined space rules require atmospheric testing before entry; a permit is required when a serious recognized hazard exists.
